Goal: hold current hypertrophy gains and maintain strength while traveling with only a yoga mat and a door pull-up bar. Use a mix of bodyweight and minimal equipment (pull-ups, door rows, tempo work, isometrics) to preserve muscle mass and performance. Structure emphasizes enough stimulus to prevent detraining, coupled with recovery and nutrition guidance to support maintenance.

Assumptions
- Access: hotel room, yoga mat, door pull-up bar.
- Frequency: 4 days/week training (Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat) over 2 weeks, with optional mobility/conditioning days if energy allows.
- Primary goals: maintain muscle mass, maintain upper/lower body strength, preserve hypertrophy signals, and sustain movement quality.
- Training time per session: 40–60 minutes.

General guidelines
- Rep ranges: 6–12 reps for most sets to preserve muscle mass; include occasional lower-rep strength work (4–6 reps) for key movements if possible.
- Tempo: control eccentric phase (3–4 seconds) to maximize time under tension with limited load.
- RPE target: 7–8/10 for main work to avoid overtraining in travel.
- Rest: 60–90 seconds between sets for hypertrophy movements; 2–3 minutes for multi-joint pull/push strength blocks.
- Warm-up: 5–8 minutes dynamic warm-up plus movement-specific activation.
- Progression: maintain or slightly increase reps/quality from week to week, but prioritize form and consistency over adding difficulty.

2-Week Travel Maintenance Plan (week-by-week)

Week 1

Day 1 — Push-focused (Chest/Shoulders/Triceps)
- Warm-up: 5–8 minutes dynamic shoulder, chest, and thoracic mobility; push-up plus mobility.
- Push-ups (door frame incline or standard depending on ability)
  - 4 sets x 8–12 reps (control tempo 2s up, 3s down)

  - 3 sets x 6–10 reps

  - 3 sets x 8–12 reps

  - 2 sets x 20–30 seconds

Day 2 — Pull-focused (Back/Biceps)

- Pull-ups or chin-ups
  - 4 sets x as many reps as possible (AMRAP) with proper form; if needed use assisted variation by holding at top briefly or performing negatives

  - 3 sets x 8–12 reps
- Doorway hinge rows or horizontal pulls on bar
  - 3 sets x 8–12 reps
- Isometric pull-up hold at top (or mid) position

Day 3 — Active Recovery / Mobility

Here’s a simple, travel-friendly approach for eating on travel days using restaurants and room service. It keeps protein high, supports maintenance, and minimizes decision fatigue.

Key goals
- Protein: aim for 1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight per day. At her weight, that’s roughly 100–150+ g protein daily.
- Energy: eat at maintenance or slight surplus to spare muscle; if appetite is suppressed, prioritize protein and adjust carbs/fats.
- Balance: include vegetables/fruit for micronutrients and fiber; choose mostly minimally processed options when possible.
- Consistency: don’t skip meals; if scheduling is tight, add a high-protein snack.

Simple go-to strategies
- Build meals around a protein source, a starch or carb source, and veggies.
- Choose lean proteins first; add whole-food carbs when available.
- Hydration: keep a water bottle handy; aim for first 1–2 liters with meals.

Room-service / restaurant guidelines
- Breakfast options:
  - Greek yogurt or egg-based dishes (omelet, scrambled eggs) with veggies.
  - Egg-white or whole egg omelet with vegetables; add a side of fruit.
  - Oatmeal with protein add-in (protein powder if available, or add milk/Greek yogurt) and berries.
- Lunch/dinner options:
  - Protein-forward mains: grilled chicken/fish/tofu/legumes, with a side of vegetables and a starch (rice, quinoa, potatoes) or whole-grain bread.
  - Stir-fries or bowls with a protein source, vegetables, and a moderate portion of rice or noodles.
  - Salads with a solid protein (chicken, tuna, shrimp, eggs) and a olive oil-based dressing; add avocado or nuts for healthy fats.
- Snacking/mini meals (in-room or on the go):
  - Protein-rich snacks: Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, edamame, boiled eggs (if available), Jerky (choose low-sodium if possible).
  - Convenience: protein bars with minimal added sugar, a fruit, a handful of nuts.
- Portion control and cues:
  - Half-plate rule: half vegetables, one-quarter protein, one-quarter starch or whole grain.
  - If protein portion is small, add an extra protein-rich snack or order a second protein item (e.g., add a side of salmon or extra eggs).
- Beverages:
  - Water > sugary drinks. If you want variety: unsweetened tea, black coffee, or sparkling water.
- Fiber and satiety:
  - Choose vegetables/fruit with meals; consider a salad or veggie side with every meal to boost fiber and fullness.

Macro-friendly restaurant templates (for quick ordering)
- Template A (Protein + Veg + Carbs)
  - Grilled chicken or fish, steamed or roasted vegetables, brown rice or quinoa; add olive oil or avocado if dressing is light.
- Template B (Bowl style)
  - Base: brown rice or quinoa; Protein: chicken, tofu, or seafood; Veg: multiple vegetables; Sauce: light or olive oil-based; Optional: avocado, beans, or nuts.
- Template C (Salad + Protein)
  - Large greens + protein (grilled chicken, tuna, shrimp); add a grain or beans; olive oil/vinegar dressing on the side.

What to avoid or limit
- Deep-fried items and heavy cream sauces frequent additions.
- Large refined-carbohydrate desserts or oversized portions that push calorie intake well above maintenance.
- High-sodium items if fluid retention is a concern.

Hydration and timing
- Protein intake spread across 3–4 meals, aiming for ~25–40 g protein per meal.
- If you’re exercising on travel days, try to have a protein-rich meal within 60–90 minutes post-workout.
- Keep a water intake goal (e.g., 2–3 liters daily) and adjust for climate and activity.

- Breakfast: Omelet with 2–3 eggs, egg whites, spinach, peppers; side fruit; coffee or tea.
- Lunch: Grilled chicken bowl with 1 cup cooked quinoa, mixed vegetables, and olive oil-based dressing.
- Snack: Greek yogurt with berries; or a protein shake + a piece of fruit.

- Optional late snack: Cottage cheese or a handful of nuts.

- If appetite is low, keep protein options high-protein and include a protein-rich snack with every meal.
- If dining windows are limited, bulk up meals with a protein-packed starter (e.g., a cup of lentil soup or a Greek yogurt parfait) and choose a protein-forward main.
- If uncertain about portions, ask for protein-first meals (e.g., “Could I have the chicken/fish with extra vegetables and a side of oats or potatoes?”).

A sensible weekly metric for a hold (maintenance) phase should be simple, objective, and tightly linked to what you’re trying to preserve: muscle mass, strength, and body composition, plus overall training consistency. Here are two practical options you can choose from (or combine):

Option A: Minimal weekly quantitative targets (easy to track)
- Training consistency: 4 sessions per week completed (Mon/Tue/Thu/Sat) with at least 30–40 minutes each.
- Reps/quality check: maintain or improve average rep quality on main lifts (no drop more than 1–2 reps per set from the prior week) for the primary push, pull, and lower-body movements.
- Body weight validation: ±1–2 kg around baseline body weight if available; otherwise track weight trend only if measured the same time of day.
- Sleep: average 7–9 hours per night; aim for at least 6 nights of solid sleep per week.
- Perceived exertion: hold average RPE of 7–8 on main sets across the week.

Option B: Quick composite metric (single-score weekly)
- Create a simple weekly score by combining:
  - Training adherence: 1 point per session completed (max 4).
  - Strength maintenance: 1 point if you maintain or improve the average tempo/technique quality on 2–3 key movements (e.g., push-up quality, pull-up form, squat depth) compared to the previous week.
  - Body weight stability: 1 point if weight stays within ±2% of baseline; 0 if outside range.
  - Sleep quality: 1 point if average nightly sleep ≥7 hours; 0 otherwise.
  - Total weekly score: add up to 4 points. 4/4 is ideal maintenance week; 3/4 acceptable; ≤2 indicates need to re-check volume, recovery, or nutrition.

Practical implementation tips
- Pick 1–2 precise metrics to log each week to keep it simple. Commonly:
  - Training adherence (yes/no per session).
  - One strength/quality metric (e.g., ability to complete push-up reps with tempo as prescribed, or hold time in an isometric).
  - Body weight measurement (same scale, same time of day, ideally after waking and bathroom).
- Use a lightweight tracking sheet (even a one-page note) or a quick spreadsheet: date, session, reps completed, RPE, weight, sleep hours, and a brief note on recovery or fatigue.
- Set a weekly review moment (e.g., every Sunday) to assess the score and decide if any adjustments are needed (slightly reduce volume if fatigue high, ensure protein target met, adjust hydration).

Here is a side-by-side summary of the full 2-week travel plan, all bodyweight-only, with the Week 2 updates (harder) clearly shown next to Week 1. Each week has 4 training days (Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat) plus 15-minute cardio finishers on Days 1, 2, and 4, and an optional mobility/activation Day 3.

Week 1 (baseline)

Day 1 — Push: Chest/Shoulders/Triceps
- Warm-up: 5–8 min mobility
- Push-ups: 4 sets x 8–12 reps (2s up, 3s down)
- Pike push-ups / elevated push-ups: 3 sets x 6–10 reps
- Triceps press (door frame): 3 sets x 8–12 reps
- Isometric mid-range push-up hold: 2 sets x 20–30 sec
- Core: hollow hold / dead bug: 3 sets x 20–30 sec
- 15-min cardio finisher (rotate options)
  - A: 30s max push-up-to-pull-up transitions x 15 rounds
  - B: 45s high-knee in place x 15 rounds
  - C: 1-min brisk mountain climbers x 15 rounds

Day 2 — Pull: Back/Biceps
- Warm-up: scapular activation
- Pull-ups/Chin-ups: 4 sets x AMRAP
- Inverted rows under door frame: 3 sets x 8–12 reps
- Isometric pull-up hold: 2 sets x 15–20 sec
- Biceps work (towel curls or isometrics): 2 sets x 10–12 reps or 15–20s hold
- Core: side plank 3 sets x 20–30 sec per side
- 15-min cardio finisher
  - A: 4 rounds x 1 min fast feet + 30 sec rest
  - B: 6 rounds of 60s continuous rope-like movement (imaginary rope)
  - C: 15 rounds of 60s tempo rows (no weight)

Day 3 — Mobility / Active Recovery
- 20–30 min mobility
- Optional 15–20 min light cardio
- 10–15 min breathwork or short yoga flow

Day 4 — Lower Body/Glutes/Hamstrings
- Warm-up: hip hinge prep
- Tempo squats: 4 sets x 8–12 reps; 3s down
- Hip hinge pattern: floor bridge march / glute bridges: 3–4 sets x 12–15 reps
- Split squats / bulgarians: 3 sets x 8–12 reps per leg
- Step-ups or calf-taps: 3 sets x 12–15 reps per leg
- Core: marching planks or dead bug
- 15-min cardio finisher
  - A: 5 rounds of 1-min sprint-in-place + 1-min easy jog
  - B: 3 rounds of 2-min stair climbs + 1-min rest
  - C: 10 rounds of 45s burpees + 15s rest

Week 2 (updated to be a bit harder)

Day 1 — Push: Progression (Harder)
- Warm-up: 5–8 min mobility
- Decline push-ups / archer progress: 4 sets x 9–13 reps
- Pike push-ups / wall handstand progress: 4 sets x 6–10 reps
- Triceps dips: 4 sets x 9–12 reps
- Isometric hold at lower push-up: 2 sets x 25–35 sec
- Core: hollow body hold / long lever plank: 3 sets x 30–40 sec
- 15-min cardio finisher (rotate options)
  - A: 20 rounds of 20s sprint tempo/40s easy
  - B: 2 rounds of 3 min total work (1.5 min fast, 1.5 min slow)
  - C: 4 rounds of 60s tempo push-ups + 30s rest

Day 2 — Pull: Strength Emphasis (Harder)
- Warm-up: scapular activation
- Pull-ups/Chin-ups: 4 sets x AMRAP (increase reps from Week 1)
- Inverted rows: 4 sets x 8–12 reps
- Isometric top hold: 2 sets x 20–25 sec
- Biceps work: towel curls holds / isometrics: 2–3 sets x 12–15 reps or 20–25s holds
- Core: anti-rotation (plank with shoulder row or side plank with reach): 3 sets x 10–12 reps/side
- 15-min cardio finisher
  - A: 5 rounds of 45s fast feet / 15s rest
  - B: 6 rounds of 60s continuous rope-like motion (imaginary rope) / 30s rest
  - C: 15 rounds of 45s tempo rows in motion (no weight)

Day 3 — Mobility / Light Conditioning
- 20–30 min mobility
- Optional 15–20 min light cardio
- 10 min mobility flow

Day 4 — Lower Body / Glutes / Posterior Chain (Harder)
- Warm-up: hip hinge prep
- Tempo squats: 4 sets x 9–13 reps; 3s down
- Hip hinge: glute bridge march / single-leg glute bridge with tempo 3–4s down: 4 sets x 12–16 reps
- Bulgarian split squats / lunges: 4 sets x 8–12 reps per leg
- Step-ups / calf-elevated step-taps: 3–4 sets x 12–15 reps per leg
- Core: RFE leg lowers / dead bug with tempo: 3–4 sets x 10–12 reps per side
- 15-min cardio finisher
  - A: 6 rounds of 30s max-effort march-in-place, 30s rest
  - B: 3 rounds of 2 min brisk stairs, 1 min rest
  - C: 4 rounds of 90s continuous tempo squats in place, 30s rest

Active recovery Day (as needed)
- If fatigue arises, swap Day 4 with the Week 1 lower-day template or Day 3-like mobility block to ensure recovery.

Key points
- Finishers: 15-minute cardio finishers remain in both weeks, with Week 2 finishers slightly more challenging (greater tempo, more rounds, or longer continuous segments).
- Tempo and quality: Week 2 emphasizes smoother tempo, slightly higher total reps, and deeper control to convey progress without external weights.
- Recovery and nutrition remain aligned with the plan: protein targets, hydration, sleep, and maintenance calories to hold gains.

If you want, I can convert this into a compact two-column printable cheat sheet (Week 1 on the left, Week 2 on the right) with exact sets/reps/tempo and the 15-minute cardio finisher options for quick reference on travel days.
